content.text:
I found five em dashes and a handful of other AI tells. Most of the copy is in [page.tsx](app/page.tsx), plus a few lines in `layout.tsx` and `StepArt.tsx`.

## Em dashes (5)
- [layout.tsx:9](app/layout.tsx:9): the page title, "Earshot — live AI captions for any video"
- [page.tsx:67](app/page.tsx:67): "…any video that plays in the page — no YouTube captions required."
- [page.tsx:100](app/page.tsx:100): "…press Share — and only that tab."
- [page.tsx:177](app/page.tsx:177): "Captions appear as words are spoken — usually in under a second."
- [StepArt.tsx:56](components/StepArt.tsx:56): "Earshot asks Chrome to listen to this tab — nothing else."

## Other copy smells
- **A dramatic add-on after the dash.** "— and only that tab" and "— nothing else" have the same shape: a point, then an emphatic reassurance tacked on. Together they say the same thing twice.
- **A cute parallel headline.** "Your audio, your call" ([page.tsx:98](app/page.tsx:98)) is a very common AI section title.
- **Lists of three everywhere:**
  - "search, click to jump back, and download" (line 38)
  - "Any YouTube video, Short or livestream" (line 74)
  - "searchable, clickable transcript" in the meta description
- **"No X required"** (line 68) is a stock tagline phrase.
- **Hype filler words:**
  - "right here in Earshot's player" (line 74)
  - "right on youtube.com" (line 112)
  - "ends it instantly" (line 103)
  - "powered by Deepgram Nova-3" in the meta description
- **An overclaim the page then walks back.** The headline says "for **any** video." Line 112 says some videos can't be played outside YouTube, and the footer says it only works in Chrome and Edge on desktop. The "AI" in the headline is also buzzwordy, since nobody picks captions because they're AI.
- **The product as a person.** "Earshot listens along" and "Earshot hears the video" turn the app into a character. "Transcripts live in your browser tab" does the same.
- **The same line twice.** "Paste a YouTube video or livestream" appears in both the hero (line 38) and the meta description.

## Layout and design smells
- **The default AI landing page structure:** a hero with a big headline, a subhead and an input; then a "How it works" section with three numbered steps and illustration cards; then a two-card grid; then a two-item footer.
- **The default styling:** a dark theme with one warm accent color, `rounded-3xl` cards with a 1px ring, a radial gradient behind the preview, and a pulsing "Live captions" badge. Bricolage Grotesque with Inter is also a font pairing that AI tools reach for constantly.
- **Developer instructions in a card for visitors.** The extension card ([page.tsx:115-128](app/page.tsx:115)) gives `npm run build` steps. That reads like a README pasted into the page, not something a visitor can act on.

## What isn't a problem
- The curly quotes and the "Try one:" example chips are fine.
- The caption preview that writes itself in is a real, specific detail. Keep it.

content.text:
Nothing's edited yet. Here's what I'd change each line to, so you can approve or redline first.

**Page title** ([layout.tsx:9](app/layout.tsx:9))
- Before: Earshot — live AI captions for any video
- After: Earshot: live captions for YouTube

**Meta description**
- Before: Paste a YouTube video or livestream and get real-time captions and a searchable, clickable transcript, powered by Deepgram Nova-3.
- After: Live captions and a transcript for YouTube videos and streams that don't have captions.

**Hero headline**
- Before: Live AI captions for any video.
- After: Captions for videos that don't have them.

**Hero subhead**
- Before: Paste a YouTube video or livestream. Earshot listens along and writes captions as people speak, plus a transcript you can search, click to jump back, and download.
- After: Paste a YouTube link and captions show up as people talk. You also get a transcript. Click any line to jump back to that moment.

**How it works intro** (line 67)
- Before: Earshot hears the video through Chrome's tab sharing, so it works with any video that plays in the page — no YouTube captions required.
- After: It uses Chrome's tab sharing to hear the video's audio. The video doesn't need captions of its own.

**Step 1** (line 74)
- Before: Any YouTube video, Short or livestream. It plays right here in Earshot's player.
- After: Videos, Shorts and livestreams all work. The video plays on this page.

**Step 2** ([StepArt.tsx:56](components/StepArt.tsx:56))
- Before: Earshot asks Chrome to listen to this tab — nothing else.
- After: Chrome will ask which tab to share.

**Privacy card heading** (line 98)
- Before: Your audio, your call
- After: Privacy

**Privacy bullets**
- Before: Earshot only hears a tab after you pick it and press Share — and only that tab.
- After: Earshot can only hear the tab you share.
- Before: Audio streams to Deepgram for transcription while captions are on. Stop captions, or Chrome's "Stop sharing", ends it instantly.
- After: While captions are on, the audio goes to Deepgram to be transcribed. Stopping captions, or clicking "Stop sharing" in Chrome, cuts it off.
- Before: Transcripts live in your browser tab and disappear when you close it. Nothing is stored on a server.
- After: Transcripts aren't saved anywhere. Close the tab and they're gone.

**Caption preview note** (line 177)
- Before: Captions appear as words are spoken — usually in under a second.
- After: Captions usually show up less than a second after someone speaks.

**Extension card** (lines 110–128)
- Before: the "Captions on youtube.com itself" heading, a short pitch, then three `npm run build` steps.
- After: keep the heading and one sentence: "Some videos won't play outside YouTube. The Chrome extension captions them on youtube.com." Then add a "Setup instructions" link to the README instead of the build steps.

**Footer:** no change. It's already plain.

Two choices for you:
1. **The headline.** "Captions for videos that don't have them" says why someone would use Earshot. If you'd rather it say what Earshot is, "Live captions for YouTube" is the safer option.
2. **The layout.** These rewrites change the words only. I could also break up the template structure (hero, three steps, two cards), but that's a bigger change.
